blocks.heading: Write the warning once
blocks.body:
A **conref** is a pointer that pulls a chunk from another file by **path plus id**.

Today you feel the path form. The library file holds the note. The how-to points at it. Author shows the words. Text shows the pointer.

**Reusable Components** view lists chunks from the root map. Insert from there if you have it. Do not paste the sentence.

blocks.heading: Do the work
blocks.body:
You just met the idea. Now do the lab: One warning, one pointer.

This lab can fail. Fail when: The warning sentence is copied into the how-to, or there is no pointer, or the library page is a chapter in the table of contents.

Expected: One source sentence. The how-to shows it through a pointer. Text has no copy. Completeness is clean after repair.

blocks.lead: Walk the cards below, in order, to One warning, one pointer.
blocks.intro: How to One warning, one pointer. Walk the cards in order. Tick them in the lab after you actually do them.

steps.title: One warning, one pointer
steps.body: This is the whole move. The next cards are the steps, in order.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.body: Create topics/library/warnings.dita (an explaining page is fine). One warning note with id="pinch-hazard": pinch hazard at the lever. That sentence lives only in this file.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.body: Add the library page to the booklet. Hide it from the table of contents (toc="no" on the pointer, or the similar control your version shows). Write which setting you used.

image.alt: New document wizard in Oxygen XML Editor
image.caption: File > New. Pick a file type here. On day 1 you only need a blank project, not this wizard yet.
image.credit: Oxygen XML Editor User Guide, Syncro Soft

steps.title: Step 3
steps.body: In prime-the-pump.dita, insert a note that points at that warning (conref to warnings.dita, id pinch-hazard). Use Reusable Components view if you have it.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.body: Author should show the warning text. Text should show the pointer, not a second copy of the sentence.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.body: Typo the path on the pointer. Author shows a broken pull. Write the message. Put the path back.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.body: Do not paste the warning sentence into the how-to as a backup paragraph.

blocks.summary: One source sentence. The how-to shows it through a pointer. Text has no copy. Completeness is clean after repair.

blocks.body: The lab is done. Prove it with the check. Use words from today only.

blocks.lead: Answer with words from today only.
blocks.q: A warning pointer uses a path plus an id. What is the id on?
options: The file name without a suffix
The note (the chunk) you want to pull
The product name in the booklet
blocks.why: The path finds the file. The id finds the note inside it.

blocks.lead: Answer with words from today only.
blocks.q: Reusable Components view is empty. First place you look?
options: Whether the root map is set and the library page is in that booklet
blocks.why: The view reads the booklet. No root map, no library list.
